phase3.openingDialogue: Inter-thread communication — talk to your threads! 💬

mcq.question:
Why does this lesson's produce()/consume() code use `while (available)` around wait(), instead of `if (available)`?

A) while loops are always faster than if statements in Java
B) A woken thread must re-check the condition — another thread could've changed it first
C) It's required syntax — wait() only compiles inside a while loop
D) It has no real effect; if would work identically here

phase4.selfChallenge:
Create a simple producer-consumer program:
1. SharedBuffer class with capacity of 5
2. produce(int value) — adds value, waits if full
3. consume() — removes value, waits if empty
4. Create one producer thread (produces 10 items)
5. Create one consumer thread (consumes 10 items)
6. Print each produce/consume action

Use wait/notifyAll for synchronization.

phase5.trivia: wait()/notify() sit on Object, not Thread — every single object in Java, from a String to a custom class, technically has a built-in monitor capable of this coordination, whether or not it's ever actually used that way.
